content.text: {"primary_meaning": "In mainstream Christian teaching, 'stone' (and the closely related 'rock') most commonly symbolizes Jesus Christ himself, especially as the rejected stone that becomes the cornerstone/foundation of God's building (the church), and simultaneously as a stone of stumbling for unbelievers. The New Testament writers explicitly apply the Old Testament 'stone' texts christologically, and this reading has been dominant from the patristic era onward.", "primary_basis": ["Psalm 118:22 (the stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone)", "Isaiah 28:16 (a tested, precious cornerstone laid in Zion)", "Isaiah 8:14 (a stone of stumbling, a rock of offense)", "Daniel 2:34-35, 44-45 (the stone cut without hands that destroys the statue and becomes a great mountain, read christologically/messianically)", "Matthew 21:42-44 and parallels (Mark 12:10-11; Luke 20:17-18)", "Acts 4:11 (Peter applies Psalm 118:22 to Jesus)", "Romans 9:32-33 (stumbling stone in Zion applied to Christ)", "Ephesians 2:20 (Christ Jesus himself the cornerstone)", "1 Peter 2:4-8 (the living stone, cornerstone, and stone of stumbling all applied to Christ)", "1 Corinthians 10:4 (the rock that followed Israel was Christ)"], "alternatives": [{"meaning": "Believers as 'living stones' built into a spiritual house/temple upon Christ the cornerstone \\u2014 the church as God's building.", "basis": ["1 Peter 2:5", "Ephesians 2:19-22", "1 Corinthians 3:9-17"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "God himself as 'the Rock' \\u2014 a title of stability, refuge, and faithfulness (often merged with the christological reading but originally a divine epithet).", "basis": ["Deuteronomy 32:4, 15, 18", "Psalm 18:2, 31", "Psalm 62:2, 6-7", "2 Samuel 22:2-3"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "Peter as the rock on which the church is built \\u2014 dominant in Roman Catholic interpretation; Protestant traditions often read the rock as Peter's confession or as Christ, making this a materially contested reading.", "basis": ["Matthew 16:18"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "Stones as memorials or witnesses \\u2014 standing stones, altars, and cairns commemorating covenant events (Bethel, Gilgal, Ebenezer).", "basis": ["Genesis 28:18-22", "Joshua 4:1-9, 20-24", "Joshua 24:26-27", "1 Samuel 7:12"], "prominence": "minority"}, {"meaning": "Stone as hardness/deadness of the human heart, contrasted with a heart of flesh in regeneration.", "basis": ["Ezekiel 11:19", "Ezekiel 36:26", "2 Corinthians 3:3", "Zechariah 7:12"], "prominence": "minority"}, {"meaning": "Stone tablets of the Law \\u2014 stone representing the old covenant written externally, contrasted with the Spirit writing on hearts.", "basis": ["Exodus 31:18", "2 Corinthians 3:3, 7"], "prominence": "minority"}, {"meaning": "The 'white stone' with a new name given to the overcomer \\u2014 variously read as acquittal, admission (tessera), or personal acceptance by Christ; no agreed interpretation.", "basis": ["Revelation 2:17"], "prominence": "unclear"}, {"meaning": "The Daniel 2 stone read specifically as the kingdom of God (rather than Christ personally) crushing worldly empires \\u2014 emphasized in some eschatological traditions (e.g., historicist and Latter-day Saint readings).", "basis": ["Daniel 2:34-35, 44-45"], "prominence": "minority"}], "has_settled_consensus": true, "confidence": "high", "notes": "Consensus is strong because the New Testament itself performs the interpretation: Jesus, Peter, and Paul all quote the Old Testament stone texts (Psalm 118:22; Isaiah 8:14; 28:16) and apply them directly to Christ, and 1 Peter 2:4-8 gathers all three into a single christological catena. The main genuine interpretive divergence concerns Matthew 16:18 (Peter vs. Peter's confession vs. Christ), which is a confessional dividing line rather than a challenge to the broader Christ-as-cornerstone consensus. Secondary meanings (living stones, memorial stones, stony hearts, tablets of law) are widely acknowledged but treated as distinct sub-motifs rather than rivals to the primary meaning."}
